subject: Re: Hosted API - temporary p95 relief & routing policy for Finera
messages:
From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@finera.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Finera Ops <ops@finera.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API p95 — request for temporary relief and routing details

Hi Karthik / Jordan,

We're seeing a concentrated migration cutover next week that will spike our request fanout for ~48 hours. Our SREs expect sustained p95 latency breaches for a short window as clients warm caches and traffic fans out. Procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a short-term SLO exception or a traffic-routing allowance so we don't hit penalty thresholds while we run the migration.

Can you send a proposed exception path (duration, measurement window change, rollback criteria) and any routing/fallback policy you recommend? Also list any collateral or audit artifacts procurement will need to sign off.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Liu
Head of Infrastructure, Finera
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@finera.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API p95 — request for temporary relief and routing details

Tom —

Appreciate the heads up. We can support a temporary, scoped adjustment while you run the migration. High-level proposal below:

- Exception window: 14 days starting the first day of your cutover, with the option to extend once by 7 days upon joint review.
- Measurement: During the exception, we will evaluate p50/p95 on a 1-hour sliding window for internal telemetry, but contractual relief will be applied to a 24-hour aggregation to avoid transient noise.
- Scope: Relief applies only to p95 latency for the Hosted API in us-west region and does not change uptime commitments.
- Mitigations we’ll enable:
  * Prefix caching warm-up (estimated benefit for your flows)
  * Route burst traffic to higher-priority pool with temporary burst credits (no additional charge for the first 72 hours of the cutover)
  * Enable transient bypass routing: requests that exceed X ms will be re-routed to a lower-latency model variant with higher throughput.
- Rollback criteria: If p95 > 2x baseline for more than 48 consecutive hours after day 3 of the window, we’ll convene an incident review and revert routing changes.

I’ve attached a short evidence packet that procurement asked for in past deals — contains how we measure p95 (aggregation method), instrumentation sample, and historical precedents. Also attaching a diff file for the routing change we’d apply.

If this looks acceptable in principle, we can draft a 1-page addendum for signatures and a timeline that lists the technical owners and runbook tasks. LMK and we’ll schedule a 30-min alignment call.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@finera.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API p95 — request for temporary relief and routing details

Quick technical notes to complement Karthik's proposal:

- Prefix/KV cache warm-up: we recommend seeding the most-used prefixes 24–48 hours before cutover. We can run a warmup job on your behalf if you provide the sample query set.
- Measurement detail: Our hosted p95 calculation excludes queued retries and uses request arrival timestamps at the front-door; during the exception we'll also provide a "raw p95" trace so your SREs can correlate.
- Routing policy: the temporary variant will include a soft-throttle at the proxy level and an emergency fallback model. This will reduce latency spikes but may change token-cost profile; we'll surface cost delta in the runbook.

I've attached routing-policy-diff.txt with the exact config changes (proxy weights, TTLs, and initial throttle thresholds).

If procurement wants the shortest addendum possible, we can convert the operational bullets into acceptance criteria and an automated expiry clause.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@finera.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Finera Ops <ops@finera.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API p95 — request for temporary relief and routing details

Karthik / Jordan —

Thanks for the clear proposal. Finera is willing to accept a scoped exception under these conditions: 14-day window with a one-time 7-day extension, documented rollback criteria, and the warm-up plan executed by Redwood. Procurement needs the one-page addendum and the evidence packet to attach to our change request.

Please:
- Send the draft addendum for legal/procurement review (we prefer a single-page exhibit).
- Confirm who at Redwood will run the seed/warm-up job and provide a contact.
- Share the script or job spec for the warm-up so our SREs can mirror it in pre-prod.

We will aim to start the cutover on Sep 1; procurement will target sign-off by Aug 28 if they have the addendum.

Tom
Tom Liu
Head of Infrastructure, Finera

To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@finera.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API p95 — request for temporary relief & routing policy for Finera

Tom —

Great — I'll circulate the addendum draft and the warm-up job spec right now. Action items and owners below:

1) Draft addendum (Karthik) — circulating in 60 minutes, includes:
   - Exception dates: Sep 1 — Sep 14 (opt +7d)
   - Measurement: contractual relief applied to daily aggregates; internal monitoring will use 1-hour sliding windows
   - Rollback & review criteria
   - Signatures: Finera Head of Infrastructure + Redwood Director of Prod Partnerships
2) Warm-up job & script (Jordan) — deliverables: job spec, sample queries, and runbook steps by EOD Aug 27
3) On-call contact for cutover (Laura) — will be primary point for Redwood execs during the window; contact info in addendum
4) Procurement packet (Marissa) — provide SLO evidence PDF and historical precedent doc; cc procurement@finera.com when sending

Links: HubSpot record and Drive folder (shared). I will also create the DocuSign room for the addendum (link in Drive).

Attachment: finera-temp-addendum-draft.docx (draft).

We’ll plan a 30-min alignment call for Aug 27 4:00pm PT — sending calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you across the finish line.

—Karthik
